sentences: Revolving credit utilization is the most important driver of default risk, accounting for about 38% of the model's importance, and risk rises steeply as utilization climbs, especially above about 70% of the credit limit.
The number of past delinquencies is a strong driver, and having at least one delinquency raises the predicted risk compared with having none.
Annual income is a moderate to strong driver, and risk falls as income rises, with the largest drop between the lower and middle income bands.
The effect of utilization is essentially the same whether the applicant has a short or long credit history, so the two do not meaningfully interact.
Length of credit history has at most a weak effect, with longer histories associated with slightly lower risk.
The data do not settle whether the debt-to-income ratio has any effect on risk at this sample size.
Age, recent credit inquiries, and the two unnamed application attributes each hardly matter for the model's predictions.
The remaining interactions, between income and the application attributes or age, and between utilization and debt-to-income, are too small to matter in practice.
